articles.title: Microsoft's worst 'Nightmare' unleashes BitLocker bypass 0-day
articles.summary: ShinyHunters pwned 100+ organizations using an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day because apparently enterprise security is still stuck in 2005. Universities got hit hardest, proving that higher education means lower security standards.

articles.title: VRChat says somebody faked a breach notice with the Maine AG's office
articles.summary: Nightmare Eclipse strikes again with a BitLocker bypass that makes your encrypted drives about as secure as a screen door. Microsoft's nightmare just became everyone else's reality.

articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 vulnerability patches in one Patch Tuesday, proving that AI isn't just making art—it's making security researchers find bugs faster than devs can ship them. Three dozen earned the coveted 'critical' rating because why fix things right the first time?

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually published AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's a recipe for banana bread, and now Congress wants answers. Nothing says cybersecurity leadership like accidentally open-sourcing your entire secret infrastructure.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers social-engineered Meta's AI support bot to hijack Obama's Instagram account with pro-Iranian propaganda. When your AI customer service is dumber than a call center in 1995, maybe it's time to reconsider automation.

articles.title: Cybercriminals claim breach of Oracle PeopleSoft servers at 100-plus organizations | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nearly a million passports and IDs were just sitting on the public internet waiting to be harvested like digital fruit. Because apparently 'security through obscurity' means hoping nobody types random URLs into their browser.

articles.title: Phishing Attack Volume Down 20%, but Risk Still Rising
articles.summary: Congress keeps kicking the Section 702 surveillance can down the road while civil liberties hang in the balance. Either add a warrant requirement or watch democracy get NSA'd into oblivion.

articles.title: ‘News’ Site Keeps Hallucinating EFF Staffers
articles.summary: California wants to ban surveillance pricing—where corporations stalk your digital footprints to charge you custom ripoff rates. Finally, someone realizes that behavioral targeting isn't just creepy marketing, it's algorithmic price discrimination.

articles.title: Lawmakers Demand Answers as CISA Tries to Contain Data Leak
articles.summary: Netherlands seized 800 servers and arrested two hosting company owners for enabling Russian cyberattacks on the EU. Sometimes the good guys actually win one, even if it took them way too long to connect the dots.

articles.title: Nearly a million passports and photo IDs were left unprotected on the public internet
articles.summary: Nightmare Eclipse dropped a seventh Windows zero-day hours after Microsoft threatened criminal prosecution, because nothing motivates a researcher quite like corporate legal intimidation. The legend continues with SYSTEM privileges for everyone.
